h1: Traditional Indian Games in the Playground: Unt Sawari, Fugdi, Stapu and More

props.title: Traditional Indian Games in the Playground: Unt Sawari, Fugdi, Stapu and More
props.summaryText: How games Indian children have played for generations, from unt sawari and fugdi to stapu, chausar and kite flying, inspire playground equipment that feels familiar and fresh.
props.author: rohan-mehta
props.imageAlt: Children on a wooden-look slide and play structure inspired by Indian games

takeaways.text: Traditional games give children (and their grandparents) something familiar and something to talk about.
Equipment inspired by Indian games builds the same skills as any playground: balance, coordination, cooperation.
Our FunPlay Originals ranges such as Khel Khud, Timeless Play and Organic Play draw on these games and on Indian nature.
Cultural designs make a play area feel local and suit schools, parks and resorts alike.

faq.a: Stapu, also called langdi or kith-kith in different regions, is the Indian version of hopscotch: children hop through a grid of squares drawn on the ground. In a playground it can be built into a poured rubber surface or turned into a trail of hopping posts.

Unt sawari means camel ride. Children's camel rides are a familiar sight at fairs and beaches in India, and playground spring riders shaped like camels bring the same fun into a safe, everyday form. Our Organic Play range includes an Unt Savari spring rider.

faq.q: What playground equipment is inspired by Indian games?
faq.a: FunPlay's Khel Khud range is inspired by Indian games, while Timeless Play includes designs based on fugdi, chausar, paheli and patang (kites), and Wall Play includes a Dahi Handi climbing wall. Organic Play includes spring riders and structures inspired by Indian nature.
